## Read the endpoints carefully {#l3-interval-notation .interval-notation}

:::: {.split}
::: {.column-block}

### Include the lower endpoint

$$10\text{–}<20 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 10\le x<20$$

Include **10**. Exclude **20**.

```{=html}
<svg class="interval-line" viewBox="0 0 480 125" role="img" aria-label="From 10 included to 20 excluded">
<path d="M35 45H445" stroke="#81938f" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M85 45H395" stroke="#007f78" stroke-width="7"/>
<circle cx="85" cy="45" r="10" fill="#007f78"/><circle cx="395" cy="45" r="10" fill="#f7f5ef" stroke="#007f78" stroke-width="4"/>
<g font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#152e3b" text-anchor="middle"><text x="85" y="97">10</text><text x="395" y="97">20</text></g></svg>
```

:::
::: {.column-block}

### Include the upper endpoint

$$10>\text{–}20 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 10<x\le20$$

Exclude **10**. Include **20**.

```{=html}
<svg class="interval-line" viewBox="0 0 480 125" role="img" aria-label="From 10 excluded to 20 included">
<path d="M35 45H445" stroke="#81938f" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M85 45H395" stroke="#3b66a8" stroke-width="7"/>
<circle cx="85" cy="45" r="10" fill="#f7f5ef" stroke="#3b66a8" stroke-width="4"/><circle cx="395" cy="45" r="10" fill="#3b66a8"/>
<g font-family="Arial,sans-serif" font-size="27" fill="#152e3b" text-anchor="middle"><text x="85" y="97">10</text><text x="395" y="97">20</text></g></svg>
```

:::
::::

::: {.takeaway}
A filled endpoint is included. An open endpoint is excluded.
:::

::: notes
These are class-interval shorthands, not chained inequalities. Read the complete interval: $a\text{–}<b$ means $a\le x<b$; $a>\text{–}b$ means $a<x\le b$. In particular, the second form does not mean that the smaller endpoint is greater than the larger endpoint.

Ask students where 10, 15 and 20 belong under each convention. Example 3.12 retains the booklet's lower-inclusive notation. The hinge later asks students to reclassify the same observations under the other convention.
:::
